subject: maths
question: From point P, X walks at a speed of 12 km/hr and 6 hours after his start Y also starts walking from same point P on his cycle after him at the speed of 16 km/hr. How far from the starting point P will Y catch X?
solution:
**Given:**

X's speed = 12 km/hr

Y's speed = 16 km/hr

Time difference between X's and Y's start = 6 hours

**Concept:**

When Y starts, X has already covered a certain distance. Y will catch up by covering the distance X has covered plus the additional distance at a relative speed.

**Formula Used:**

Distance covered = Speed × Time

Relative speed = Speed of Y - Speed of X

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by X in 6 hours:

⇒ DistanceX = 12 km/hr × 6 hr

⇒ DistanceX = 72 km

Relative speed of Y catching up to X:

⇒ Relative speed = 16 km/hr - 12 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 4 km/hr

Time taken by Y to catch up to X:

⇒ Time = DistanceX / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 72 km / 4 km/hr

⇒ Time = 18 hours

Distance from starting point P when Y catches X:

⇒ Distance = SpeedY × Total time

⇒ Distance = 16 km/hr × (18 hours)

⇒ Distance = 288 km

**∴ The correct answer is option 2 (288 km).**
